title: Spliceboard: Prompt Heuristic Journal
content:
Quick notes / brain dump (scratch — do not share externally)

Context and intent
- Personal labbook for trying out compact few-shot template variants that trade off token budget for stability. Goal: find templates <~120 tokens that keep instruction fidelity across model variants (redwood-llama-70b-q4, rwin-3b-fp16, llama-c-13b).
- Focus areas: exemplar selection order, micro-priming lines, explicit refusal anchors, and edge-case adversarial probes.
- Hypothesis: a 3-exemplar pattern with a short canonicalization instruction + explicit format spec is most robust in low-token budgets.

To-dos (short)
- [ ] Run batch jobs for 3-template permutations (order, diversity) across temps {0.0, 0.2, 0.7}. Linear INF-914 assigned.
- [ ] Add metric hooks: exact-match for structured output, BLEU-ish for short answers, hallucination flag via regex rules.
- [ ] Get Marcus to review the exemplar selection script (utils/select_exemplars.py) — suspect sampling bias.

Notes-to-self: prompt micro-patterns that seem promising
1) Canonicalize + Fewshot + Format guard (compact)
  - Instruction intro (10–14 tokens): "Rewrite to canonical Q/A, keep labels."
  - 3 exemplars: vary length, include a deliberately incomplete case
  - Format guard (12 tokens): "Return JSON with keys: question, answer, confidence"
  - End token budget: ~100 tokens total
  - Empirical: good at preserving label names across quantized models, but confidence scoring is noisy.

2) Role anchor + Minimal exemplar + Negative exemplar
  - "You are a precise assistant. Don't add extra sentences."
  - Two positive exemplars, one negative (shows common bad output)
  - Observed: negative exemplar helps avoid creative completions but can trigger conservative truncation (model replies too terse).

3) Micro-shift scaffolding (chained micro-prompts)
  - Split into two micro-prompts separated by a delimiter: 
    [A] Provide a short rewrite
    [B] Now format as X
  - Pros: reduces instruction compound complexity; Cons: doubles tokens if repeated for many items.

Compact three-shot template (current canonical candidate)
---
INSTRUCTION: Canonicalize this user query into a JSON object with keys {"q","a","confidence"}. Keep "a" under 30 words.
EX1:
Q: "How to reset my password?"
A: "Go to Settings > Security > Reset password."
C: "0.95"
EX2:
Q: "Convert 3/4 to percent"
A: "75%"
C: "0.98"
EX3 (bad-case):
Q: "Write a long essay about trees"
A: "[BAD_OUTPUT]"
C: "0.10"
---
PROMPT: "Q: {{user_query}}\nA:"
Notes: try with and without explicit JSON wrapper lines ("Return ONLY JSON").

Failure cases observed (sampled)
- Hallucinated confidence scores (e.g., 1.23) — add clamp: "confidence must be 0.00–1.00" in instruction.
- Model appends commentary after JSON (common at high temp). Solution: stronger ending token like "END-OF-RESPONSE" and post-parse trimming.
- With quantized 4-bit variants, the negative exemplar sometimes gets mimicked instead of avoided (flip). Suspect tokenization differences cause exemplar leakage.

Adversarial probes to run (short list)
1) Ambiguous entity: "What's the address?" (contextless) — expect placeholder or ask clarifying question.
2) Malformed input: include a stray backtick and emojis — check JSON validity.
3) Instruction overload: append a second contradictory instruction at end — measure how often model follows first vs last.

Metric ideas (simple)
- Structure pass (binary): is output valid JSON and contains required keys?
- Label fidelity: exact match for short canonical answers (token-level equality).
- Safety/Noise score: fraction of responses containing extra commentary or disallowed tokens.
- Confidence sanity: check numeric range and monotonic relation to answer correctness in test sets.

Small experimental shot sets (for quick local runs)
SET A (diverse short) — 3 exemplars\- EX1: Q: "How do I enable dark mode?" -> A: "Settings > Appearance > Dark" -> C: 0.98\- EX2: Q: "Sum 12 and 7" -> A: "19" -> C: 0.99\- EX3: Q: "Explain photosynthesis in one line" -> A: "Plants convert light to chemical energy." -> C: 0.92
SET B (adversarial mixing)\- EX1: short factual\- EX2: long creative trimmed to [BAD_OUTPUT]\- EX3: neg example showing hallucination pattern (e.g., invented step-by-step commands).

Implementation notes for bench jobs
- Use streaming off for initial metric capture (streaming complicates parse).
- Add wrapper that discards anything after final closing brace for JSONs (practical but lossy).
- Post-parse: if confidence missing, impute 0.5 and mark as warn.
- Record model, quantization tag, seed, temperature, exemplar-order-id in results CSV.

Open hypotheses / research questions
- H1: A negative exemplar reduces hallucination only when it is the minority exemplar (1 of 3). If negative becomes majority, model flips to pessimistic behavior.
- H2: Explicit numeric clamps ("confidence between 0 and 1") are ignored by high-temp models unless combined with format guard.
- H3: exemplar order matters more for quantized 4-bit models than for fp16 models due to tokenization instability.

Quick experiment plan (week 1)
- Day 1: small sweep (100 cases) across 3 templates, 3 temps, rwin-3b-fp16. Collect structure pass and label fidelity.
- Day 2: run same sweep on redwood-llama-70b-q4 (quantized) to compare.
- Day 3: analyze top 10 failure cases, craft 10 adversarial probes and re-run.

Quick save of useful snippets (copy-paste)
- "Return JSON only. If you cannot answer, return {\"q\":..., \"a\":null, \"confidence\":0.00}"
- End token anchor: "END-OF-RESPONSE"
- Clamp instruction: "confidence must be a decimal between 0.00 and 1.00"

Loose reflections (notes-to-self)
- Keep playing with "negative exemplar" pattern — there's a fine line between corrective signal and priming a pattern to mimic.
- Consider using a short verification step: after main JSON output, ask model to output a 3-token checksum summarizing the answer (cheap integrity check).
- Talk to Solutions Eng about adding a server-side micro-parse layer that strips trailing commentary before downstream ingestion.

References / pointers (internal)
- See INF-914 (Linear) for experiment tracking.
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/prompt-benchmarks/pulls/72 includes the initial microshot harness.
- Slack thread: #prompt-lab (linked above) where Marcus posted the exemplar sampler output.

Misc garbage (brain dump)
- If we can get a small human eval pool to rate 200 cases on fidelity vs terseness, that would accelerate tuning.
- Wonder if we can compress exemplars using special tokens or anchors e.g., "[EX1]" to reduce token cost — might be model-dependent.

----
End of scratchpad.
Last edit: quick note to self: run the Day 1 sweep before EOD Friday so we have something to discuss in Monday sync.
